source: Direct owner clarification in current chat, 20 October 2026
owner_observation: The worker appears to have reused an older Haven implementation, possibly due to the shared name; this is an owner observation, not established causality.
owner_decision: Existing Haven code may be reused provided Haven renders the same standalone app implementations.
Standalone and Haven-embedded apps must not diverge into separate implementations.
All applicable requirements in the canonical specification remain mandatory.
Treat this as a pinned programme-wide constraint.
Where newer implementations exist, merge the older and newer work where useful and feasible.
Use the newer implementation directly when it is better; preserving the older implementation is not the goal.
implementation_invariants: One owning app surface/engine and canonical object identity/data/services across standalone and embedded hosts.
Host-aware top bars may adapt as explicitly requested; app-specific behavior and capabilities remain shared.
Audit real composition/factory routes and actual rendered surfaces; a renamed/wrapped legacy app or duplicate modern surface elsewhere does not establish compliance.
Reusing older code does not waive missing requirements or independent acceptance.
Compare actual requirements coverage, functionality, durability, integration and refinement before choosing or merging; timestamps/names alone do not establish quality.
Consolidate the chosen/merged implementation into one shared owning app surface for standalone and Haven; do not ship parallel divergent implementations.
authority: Direct owner clarification; canonical v2 remains sole general product authority.
